# Fix Breaking Hook API Signature in PocketBase

## Background
You have a custom Go backend embedding PocketBase. The project was recently upgraded to PocketBase v0.31.0, but the custom event hooks are failing to compile and run because they use the older v0.22 API signature. In PocketBase v0.23.0+, there was a major API overhaul affecting hook registration and event propagation.

## Requirements
- Update `main.go` to fix the `OnRecordBeforeCreateRequest` hook for the `posts` collection.
- The hook must use the new `.BindFunc()` registration method.
- The hook handler must accept the new event type (`*core.RecordRequestEvent`).
- The hook handler must check if the `title` is empty. If it is, return a bad request error.
- The hook handler must generate a slug from the title using `core.Slugify(title)` and set it on the record's `slug` field.
- The hook handler MUST call and return `e.Next()` to properly propagate the execution chain. If omitted, the record creation will be blocked.
- The application must compile successfully and run.

## Implementation Hints
- Review the PocketBase v0.23+ upgrade guide for Go hooks.
- Hook registration changed from `.Add()` to `.BindFunc()`.
- Event handlers now receive a generic `*core.RecordRequestEvent` instead of specific event types.
- Handlers must return `e.Next()` to continue the middleware chain.
- Use `e.BadRequestError("Title cannot be empty", nil)` for validation errors instead of standard `fmt.Errorf`.

## Background
You have a custom Go backend embedding PocketBase. The project was recently upgraded to PocketBase v0.31.0, but the custom event hooks are failing to compile and run because they use the older v0.22 API signature. In PocketBase v0.23.0+, there was a major API overhaul affecting hook registration and event propagation.

## Requirements
- Update `main.go` to fix the `OnRecordBeforeCreateRequest` hook for the `posts` collection.
- The hook must use the new `.BindFunc()` registration method.
- The hook handler must accept the new event type (`*core.RecordRequestEvent`).

struct will trigger the corresponding record validations and hooks.

including 3rd party plugins, that don't know or use your custom struct will still work as expected.

...

and then you can start the created executable with
`./myapp serve`.

# slugify package - go.rtnl.ai/x/slugify - Go Packages
created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-24, [Read more](https://pkg.go.dev/go.rtnl.ai/x/slugify)

Converts a string into a slug that contains only lowercase letters, digits, and dashes.
The slug will not begin or end with a dash and will not contain runs of multiple dashes.
The slug is not forced into being ASCII and may contain unicode characters, e.g. from other languages; however the slug is NFKD normalized, which breaks down characters into their compatibility equivalences e.g. ﬁ is decomposed into "f" and "i", or "ö" into "o".
Note that because the slug is not forced into ASCII, it is not technically URL safe.
You can percent encode the slug to ensure it's safe; otherwise you can rely on the fact that most modern browsers handle unicode in the address bar.
...
Creating slugs:
```
slugify.Slugify("Hello, World!")
// "hello-world"
slugify.Slugifyf("%s & %s", "naïve", "pretentious")
// "naive-and-pretentious
```
Validating slugs:
```
err := slugify.Validate("hello-world")
// nil
err = slugify.Validate("中文测试")

**it can be used as a framework** which enables you to write your own custom app business logic in Go or JavaScript and still have a portable backend at the end.
**Choose Extend with Go if you are already familiar with the language or have the time to learn it.** As the primary PocketBase language, the Go APIs are better documented and you'll be able to integrate with any 3rd party Go library since you'll have more control over the application flow.

# Extend with Go - Record proxy - Docs - PocketBase
created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-23, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/docs/go-record-proxy/)

The available `core.Record` and its helpers are usually the recommended way to interact with your data, but in case you want a typed access to your record fields you can create a helper struct that embeds `core.BaseRecordProxy` *(which implements the `core.RecordProxy` interface)* and define your collection fields as getters and setters.
By implementing the `core.RecordProxy` interface you can use your custom struct as part of a
`RecordQuery` result like a regular record model.
In addition, every DB change through the proxy
struct will trigger the corresponding record validations and hooks.
This ensures that other parts of your app,
including 3rd party plugins, that don't know or use your custom struct will still work as expected.
...
}
...
Accessing and modifying the proxy records is the same as for the regular records.
...
If you have an existing `*core.Record` value you can also load it into your proxy using the
`SetProxyRecord` method:
`// fetch regular record
record, err := app.FindRecordById("articles", "RECORD_ID")
if err != nil {
return err
}
// load into proxy
article := &Article{}
article.SetProxyRecord(record)`

# slugify package - github.com/mjadobson/pb-plugin-slug - Go ...
created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-27, [Read more](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/mjadobson/pb-plugin-slug)

Generate PocketBase slugs from one or more record fields.
The plugin combines configured input fields in order, normalizes the text to lowercase alphanumeric segments separated by hyphens, truncates the result to the configured length, and adds numeric suffixes when needed to keep slugs unique.
...
Build PocketBase with the plugin:
...
On startup the plugin creates a shared `_plugins` collection if it doesn't already exist.
Create or update the `slugify` row in `_plugins` with:
- `plugin_name`: `slugify`
- `enabled`: `true` or `false`
- `config`: JSON config
Example `config` value:
...
Then make sure each target collection has:
- the fields listed in `input_fields`
- a text or editor field matching `output_field`
- a single-column `UNIQUE` index on `output_field` (recommended with `WHERE output_field != ''`)
...
- Input field values are joined with spaces in config order.
- Array-like input values are flattened and joined with spaces before slugging.
- Accents are removed where possible.
...
- Repeated separators are collapsed and trimmed.
- Slugs are lowercased and truncated to `length`.

# Two feature suggestions: Field "Instructions" and "slug" field · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #3241
created: 2023-08-31, last updated: 2025-05-19, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/3241)

- When creating a field on a collection, add support for a "description" or "instructions" for the field.
This allows us to elaborate on what a field is for and specifically what it does for the end user.
It also allows us to provide an example.
Imagine a field called "phone" with a description of "The staff member's phone number to be displayed within their profile card in the format of xxx-xxx-xxxx".
This is more helpful than the user entering random values until they figure out how to satisfy the regex and also provides more detail on how it is used.
- Implement a new "slug" field that REDACTED-generates a slug based on another field, e.g.
 ```
title
```
or maybe even multiple other fields.
It would need the ability to be overridden/editable.
Maybe some other feature could accomplish this like configurable "REDACTED-populated" fields.

# how to get data by slug? · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #636
created: 2022-09-25, last updated: 2025-06-12, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/636)

No. I'll consider adding a helper in the future, but for now if you want to fetch a single record by a custom filter, you can use
…
```
@request.query.page = "1" && @request.query.perPage = "1"
```
.
I think a better way to do this would be to check if the slug is present in the filter query:
```
// doesn't work unfortunatelly
@request.query.filter ~ 'slug = "%"'
```
...
```
(this is done REDACTEDmatically only if your string doesn't have the
```
%
```
symbol defined; in the future there will be a more sophisticated checks to ensure escape sequence(s)). Or in other words, you could try:
```
@request.query.filter ~ '%slug = "%"%'
```

# Extend with Go - Routing - Docs - PocketBase
created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-25, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/docs/go-routing/)

Routing
PocketBase routing is built on top of the standard Go
`net/http.ServeMux`.
The router can be accessed via the `app.OnServe()` hook allowing you to register custom endpoints
and middlewares.
...
The `core.RequestEvent` comes with a local store that you can use to share custom data between
middlewares and the route action.
...
The official PocketBase SDKs expose the internal `send()` method that could be used to send requests
to your custom route(s).

# core package - github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core
created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-24, [Read more](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core)

Package core is the backbone of PocketBase.
It defines the main PocketBase App interface and its base implementation.
...
BaseApp implements core.App and defines the base PocketBase app structure.

# Collections
created: 2022-01-01, last updated: 2026-06-29, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/docs/collections/)

**Collections** represent your application data.
Under the hood they are backed by plain SQLite tables that are generated REDACTEDmatically with the collection **name** and **fields** (columns).
Single entry of a collection is called **record** (a single row in the SQL table).
You can manage your **collections** from the Dashboard, with the Web APIs using the client-side SDKs (*superusers only*) or programmatically via the Go/JavaScript migrations.
Similarly, you can manage your **records** from the Dashboard, with the Web APIs using the client-side SDKs or programmatically via the Go/JavaScript Record operations.
...
Currently there are 3 collection types: **Base**, **View** and **Auth**.
...
**Base collection** is the default collection type and it could be used to store any application data (articles, products, posts, etc.).
...
{"slug:REDACTEDgenerate":"abc-"}
...
will result in
...
from a predefined list.
...
type field for managing record file(s).
PocketBase stores in the database only the file name.
The file itself is stored either on the local disk or in S3, depending on your application storage settings.
...
type field for storing any serialized JSON value,

# Interface TextField - PocketBase JSVM reference
created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-03, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/jsvm/interfaces/core.TextField.html)

TextField defines "text" type field for storing any string value.
The respective zero record field value is empty string.
The following additional setter keys are available:
- "fieldName:REDACTEDgenerate" - REDACTEDgenerate field value if AutogeneratePattern is set.
For example:
```
record.Set("slug:REDACTEDgenerate", "") // [random value]
record.Set("slug:REDACTEDgenerate", "abc-") // abc-[random value]
```
...
REDACTEDgeneratePattern: string
AutogeneratePattern specifies an optional regex pattern that could
be used to generate random string from it and set it REDACTEDmatically
on record create if no explicit value is set or when the `:REDACTEDgenerate` modifier is used.
Note: the generated value still needs to satisfy min, max, pattern (if set)
...
Help is an extra text explaining what the field is about.
It is usually shown in Dashboard UI under the field input.
...
Id is the unique stable field identifier.
...
### pattern
...
Pattern specifies an optional regex pattern to match against the field value.
...
PrimaryKey will mark the field as primary key.
A single collection can have only 1 field marked as primary key.
